layers.repo: only `.crew/config.json` may set it; the global file's value is pruned on read and refused on write.
layers.both: either file may set it; the repo value wins over the machine one.
layers.both, ratchet: either file may set it, and the NARROWER of the two wins (`crew_guards.RATCHETED_KEYS`). A repo can tighten what the machine allows, never loosen it.
layers.both, widening warned: either file may set it and the repo wins, but a write that widens it is flagged (`crew_config._RATCHETED`).
layers.both, stricter wins: a personal key (`crew_guards.PERSONAL_KEYS`): either file may set it, and where both do the STRICTER value wins; a layer that is silent (absent or `null`) imposes nothing, so a machine value is your default for every repo and a repo may only narrow it.
layers.machine-arms: only the global file can turn it on (exactly `true`); a repo may only veto it with `false` (`crew_config.REPO_VETO_ONLY`).
layers.machine-only: read from the global file alone; a repo's own value is never consulted.
layers.human-only opt-out: a `humanOnly` key (`crew_humanonly`): `false` opts out only from the machine file or an untracked repo file, only after the owner types `/crew:confirm-config <change_id>` twice, and a `true` in either layer vetoes it. Not acted on by any hook yet (see the section below).

How many seconds the promote gate (`promote-gate.sh`) may run, counted from the moment its shell began, before it gives up and blocks (a hook that times out is not a block, so the gate stops itself first). null derives it from the guard's hook timeout less a 4 s margin: 16 s of the 20 s row. A number above the timeout less 2 s (18 s of 20) is clamped to that, so the setting can never let the gate outlive its hook; zero, a negative, a string or a boolean reads as null. The hook timeout is the guard's row in the dispatcher's table, not a setting.
